item.title: HEMA Updates Internal AI Assistant HAL with Model Context Protocol
item.description:
HEMA Updates Internal AI Assistant HAL with Model Context Protocol

The 100-year-old Dutch retailer HEMA has updated HAL, its internal AI assistant, by incorporating Model Context Protocol (MCP) and Amazon Bedrock AgentCore to consolidate fragmented organizational knowledge into a governed source of truth.

🔍 Overview

HEMA, which operates over 750 stores across multiple countries, utilized a technology organization of engineers, product owners, and business analysts to build a knowledge layer. The project focuses on two primary goals:

  • HAL: Consolidate fragmented knowledge into one governed source of truth.
  • MCP: Deliver that knowledge to people within the tools they already use, such as the HAL chat, Kiro, Claude, and other agents, rather than requiring them to visit separate portals.

🧩 How it works

HEMA built a knowledge layer on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, a platform used to build, connect, and optimize agents at scale. The system integrates several components:

Component Function
Model Context Protocol (MCP) Provides a standardized interface between AI clients and backend capabilities, allowing sources to be exposed as MCP tools.
Gateway Directly turns AWS Lambda functions and OpenAPI specifications into MCP tools without requiring custom MCP server code.
Identity Provides managed outbound OAuth2 (a token vault) to internal APIs and managed inbound JSON Web Token (JWT) authentication.
Runtime Hosts the internal agent, built with the Strands framework, as a container.
Memory & Guardrails Amazon Bedrock Guardrails and Memory provide content filtering and conversation memory with Dutch-language support and EU inference regions.

⚙️ Key details

  • Data Sources: The system uses a service catalog that maps people to teams, teams to services, services to APIs, and business capabilities. It also imports structured data from data-mesh tables and the product information management (PIM) engine.
  • Security: Security is anchored in Microsoft Entra ID with no AWS credentials on the client. Access control is driven by existing Active Directory groups.
  • Evolution: The first version of HAL was a self-contained assistant consisting of a Next.js web chat UI and a Strands agent packaged as a Linux/ARM64 container. The current architecture allows MCP-compatible clients to consume the same tools without custom work.

💡 Why it matters

Finding answers that previously required navigating three or four portals over an entire afternoon now happens in seconds from within a chat window or Integrated Development Environment (IDE). This architecture serves as the foundation for the next step: evolving HAL from a read-only knowledge layer into an action layer.

#HEMA #AmazonBedrock #MCP #AIagents #DigitalTransformation

Source: From portal-hopping to instant answers: HEMA’s journey with MCP and Amazon Bedrock | Amazon Web Services

item.title: BRP Deploys AI Proof‑of‑Concept to Optimize Manufacturing and Cut Costs
item.description:
BRP Deploys AI Proof‑of‑Concept to Optimize Manufacturing and Cut Costs

BRP’s Chief Information Officer Stéphane Bilodeau explains how the company used AI to tackle a manufacturing inefficiency that traditional methods could not solve.

🔍 Overview

  • AI strategy is defined as solving complex problems that are worth solving.
  • The focus is on problems where traditional approaches have not worked and where the outcome creates meaningful business value.
  • AI is treated as a strategic capability that requires strong internal teams and selective external partners.

🤖 AI Project Details

  • The team first spent time understanding the data and the process.
  • A proof of concept was built within a few weeks.
  • Weekly governance asks two questions: Is the problem still worth solving? and Can we solve it?.
  • If either answer is no, the effort stops – reasons may include insufficient data or missing technology.
  • Upon completion, finance validates the results and the business decides on deployment.

📈 Business Impact

  • The AI solution delivered a significant optimization.
  • In financial terms, significant savings were realized across all manufacturing sites.

🛠️ Implementation Approach

  • AI projects follow the broader IT principle of asking does it work? before scaling.
  • Predictability is valued: stable systems, consistent service quality, and on‑time, on‑budget delivery.
  • Success is measured by the ability to solve the problem reliably, not just by the sophistication of the AI.

💡 Why It Matters

  • The initiative shows that progress with AI is gradual but the benefits are real.
  • It acknowledges the hype cycle around AI and the expectation of immediate massive gains.
  • It highlights a major unknown: AI is the first invention capable of improving itself.
  • By embedding AI as a strategic capability, BRP strengthens its digital backbone that supports every function from design to distribution.

#BRP #AI #Manufacturing #DigitalTransformation #AIstrategy

Source: How IT is driving innovation, resilience, and AI at BRP

item.title: Jabil Leverages SAP Integration Suite to Simplify Global Supply Chain and Enable AI-Driven Planning
item.description:
Jabil Leverages SAP Integration Suite to Simplify Global Supply Chain and Enable AI-Driven Planning

Jabil, a global manufacturing company with more than 100 sites in over 30 countries, has begun using SAP Integration Suite to unify its technology landscape and lay the groundwork for AI‑driven supply‑chain insights.

🔍 Overview

  • Global footprint: >100 sites, 30‑plus countries, 140,000+ employees
  • Headquarters: St. Petersburg, Florida, USA
  • 60 years of engineering, supply‑chain, and manufacturing experience
  • Serves more than 400 of the world’s top brands
  • Existing environment: sites operate with varying process maturity, legacy systems, and localized workflows, creating data silos and limited early‑issue visibility

🛠️ How it works

  • Adopted a “simplify‑first, then‑innovate” mindset to avoid adding complexity
  • Uses SAP Integration Suite as a foundation to:
    • Connect disparate systems across all sites
    • Retire fragmented tools
    • Enable more consistent, end‑to‑end processes globally
  • Integrated workflows provide shared data visibility and reduce manual reconciliation
  • Real‑time supply‑chain event visibility supports faster disruption response and operational‑risk reduction
  • Trusted, unified data enables exploration of:
    • Predictive supply‑chain insights
    • Intelligent exception handling
    • AI‑driven planning and forecasting

💡 Why it matters

  • Simplicity at scale is identified as a competitive advantage
  • Standardizing processes and governance is pursued without disrupting existing operations
  • Modernization efforts are tied to measurable business value and operational resilience
  • Integrated, data‑driven operations shift employees from “chasing information” to acting on insights
  • Faster, data‑backed decisions improve supply‑chain agility and reduce risk

#Jabil #SAPIntegration #SupplyChainAI #DigitalTransformation

Source: Facilitating AI integration with simplicity at scale
